-----------------------------------------------
 W.P.(Crl) No.1330 of 2024  -----------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 9th day of January, 2025  JUDGMENT P.B.Suresh Kumar, J.
This writ petition is instituted seeking a writ of habeas corpus directing the respondents to produce the son of the petitioner, Predeep Kumar alias Vava alias Chakka Pradeep, who is detained in Central Prison, Viyyur in terms of Ext.P1 order issued under Section 3(1) of the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 2007 (the Act), and to set him at liberty.

entities.text: Predeep Kumar alias Vava alias Chakka Pradeep
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text:
The relief aforesaid is sought on the premise that the detention of the son of the petitioner is not in accordance with the provisions of Lawrancy vs State Of Kerala on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142792816/
2 the Act.
2. It is seen that 17 cases in which the detenu was involved have been considered by the Detaining Authority for the purpose of issuing the detention order.

The last 2025:KER:1469 prejudicial activity in which the detenu was involved is Crime No.290 of 2024 of Maranalloor Police Station registered on 07.07.2024 under Sections 189(2), 191(2), 190, 296, 74, 75(2), 76 and 115(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS).
The detenu was arrested in connection with the said case on 07.07.2024 itself and he was enlarged on bail on 26.07.2024.
The proposal for the detention under the Act was made by the competent authority on 26.07.2024 and the detention order was issued on 27.08.2024.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as also the learned Government Pleader.
4.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the detention order is vitiated by non-application of mind.

In order to substantiate the said contention, it was pointed out that even though it is recited in the impugned order that the proposal of the competent authority to detain the detenu was made on the basis that he is a "known rowdy", there is no subjective satisfaction in the detention order that he is a "known rowdy".
Instead, it was argued that the subjective satisfaction rendered by the 2025:KER:1469 detaining authority in the order of detention is that the detenu is a "known goonda".
According to the learned counsel, on that sole ground, the detenu is liable to be released.

It was also pointed out by the learned counsel that in the order of detention, it is recited that the cases in which the detenu is involved includes the case registered for offences punishable under Sections 376, 377, 384 and 394 of IPC without there being any material on record to substantiate the same.

According to the learned counsel, such a recital in the order of detention would also show that there was no application of mind at all while rendering the subjective satisfaction that it is necessary to detain the detenu under the Act for the purpose of preventing him from indulging in anti-social activities.

5. The learned Government Pleader asserted that the very proposal to detain the detenu under the Act is on the premise that he is a "known rowdy", and the order of detention is also issued on that basis.
It was conceded by the learned Government Pleader that it is recited in the operative portion of the detention order that he is a "known goonda".

According to the learned Government Pleader,
the same is only a mistake 2025:KER:1469 and the same cannot, therefore, be a ground to challenge the order of detention.

It was also submitted by the learned Government Pleader that the detenu is involved in several other cases which are not taken into account for the purpose of issuing the order of detention and it is having regard to the offences alleged against him in those cases that it is stated in the order of detention that the detenu is involved in cases including cases involving offences punishable under Sections 376, 377, 384 and 394 of IPC.
As such, according to the learned Government Pleader, the same is also not a ground to challenge the order of detention.
6. It is so fundamental that an order of preventive detention should be one issued after due application of mind.

Even though we were not very much impressed by the argument that there is no subjective satisfaction in the order that the detenu is a "known rowdy", we are inclined to hold that the recital in the order of detention that the detenu is accused in various cases including cases Lawrancy vs State Of Kerala on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142792816/
3 involving offences punishable under Sections 376, 377, 384 and 394 of IPC, is certainly a grave instance of non-application 2025:KER:1469 of mind.

sentences.text:
The argument advanced by the learned Government Pleader that the detenu is involved in several other cases which are not taken into account for the purpose of issuing the detention order, and it is having regard to the offences alleged against him in those cases that it is stated in the order of detention that the detenu is involved in cases including cases involving offences punishable under Sections 376, 377, 384 and 394 of IPC,
cannot be accepted since there is no reference about such cases in the order of detention.
Hence, we are of the view that the subjective satisfaction arrived at by the detaining authority suffers from non-application of mind, which vitiates the order of detention.
Needless to say, the detenu is entitled to be released.

7. Inasmuch as it is found that the detenu is entitled to be released on the ground discussed above, it is unnecessary to refer to and consider the remaining grounds urged by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
In the result, the writ petition is allowed and Ext.P1 order of detention is quashed.
There will be a direction that Predeep Kumar, the son of the petitioner shall, forthwith, be 2025:KER:1469 released from the Central Prison, Viyyur, if his detention is not otherwise required.
Registry will communicate the above order to the Prison Authorities concerned forthwith.
